Allah will not speak to or purify some on the Day of Resurrection, such as the garment-trailer, giver who reminds, false-oath seller, old adulterer, lying king and proud poor man.
Believers will see their Lord on Resurrection Day as clearly as sun and moon; each people follows what it worshipped, a bridge spans Hell, and many leave the Fire.
The Prophet will precede his people at the Cistern, whose drinkers never thirst, but some he knows will be kept from him, he being told they turned back after him.
At the Cistern the Prophet will plead for some people as his companions but must yield, being told he does not know what innovations they made after him.
The Cistern spans the distance between San'a and Medina, Jarba and Adhruh, or Amman and Aila; its vessels outnumber the stars, and its water, fed from Paradise, ends all thirst.
The Prophet will push crowds back from his Cistern and drive some away like stray camels; its water is whiter than milk and sweeter than honey, fed from Paradise.
On Resurrection Day Allah would give each Muslim a Jew or Christian as rescue from Hell, forgiving heavy sins, and pardon a believer's concealed faults while exposing disbelievers and hypocrites.
A bulky person on the Day of Judgement will not weigh as much as a gnat before Allah, as the verse says no balance will be set up for them.
On the Day of Resurrection people gather on a white plain, stand on the Sirat when earth and heaven are changed, and the earth becomes one bread for Paradise's people.
People will be gathered barefoot, naked and uncircumcised, too troubled to look at one another; Abraham is clothed first, and some of the Prophet's companions are taken to the left.
People will be gathered in three groups, and with the sun a mile away they will stand in sweat according to deeds, up to knees, waists, mouths or ears.
Whoever is thoroughly examined in the reckoning on the Day of Resurrection is ruined; the easy reckoning in the verse is only the presentation of deeds.
The Hour will befall the wicked; the Prophet and it were sent like joined fingers; a boy present would not grow old before it came to them; it comes suddenly.
Believers will see their Lord as clearly as sun and moon; Allah will question servants who forgot meeting Him, and a hypocrite's mouth is sealed while his limbs testify.
